metadata.audit: adversarial precision audit: IOBRpy originals vs iobrx/fast shims
metadata.protocol: Every case: ORIGINAL and FAST run in SEPARATE fresh subprocesses (quantiseq_fast monkey-patches the original module on import, so the original side never imports any fast shim). Inputs shared via parquet. cibersort: mixture written to CSV with float_format='%.17g' (the python-engine parser of the original is NOT round-trip exact, csv_roundtrip_exact=false, c-engine float_precision='round_trip' IS exact=true); the FAST receives the DataFrame returned by the exact pd.read_csv(path, sep=None, engine='python', index_col=0) call the original makes internally, so both sides see byte-identical solver inputs. PASS requires: identical index (incl. name), identical columns, identical dtypes, bitwise-equal values incl. NaN masks (max abs diff exactly 0.0). BOTH_ERROR_SAME_TYPE: both raise the same exception class. Seeds fixed in all builders.

CB6b.variant: 50-sample subset of eset_tme_stad (seed 7; degenerate 12-gene LM22 overlap)

forensic.finding: numeric divergence on degenerate input (12 LM22-overlapping genes, 235x50 mixture); QN=True: 1/50 samples differ (11 cells: 9 weights + Correlation + RMSE; weights max abs diff 6.69e-05, Correlation 3.0e-06, RMSE 6.7e-05); QN=False probe: 2/50 samples differ (23 cells, max 2.54e-04) - divergence is NOT quantile-normalization-dependent
forensic.solver_isolated: iobrx_rust.fit_nusvr_linear verified BIT-EXACT vs sklearn NuSVR (dual_coef and w identical) on all 150 (sample x nu) fits of the exact original-preprocessed CB6b inputs, and on random well-conditioned 100x22/500x22 and degenerate 12x22/16x22 problems
forensic.bisect: the failing sample alone (1 column) matches bitwise; divergence requires >=21 columns of context (5/7/11-column windows match, 21-column window diverges 4.5e-05) => cause is an N-dependent reduction inside the fast's internal preprocessing (exp2/z-score/QN-mean), not the SVR solve
forensic.extra: exposed helper iobrx_rust.quantile_normalize_np disagrees MASSIVELY with the numpy reference QN on exactly this real 235x50 matrix (every cell, max abs diff 2679) while agreeing on its 50x235 transpose, on same-shape random data (with and without injected ties), and on small cases - value-pattern-dependent bug in the exposed helper; cibersort_core itself cannot be using that broken path (CB1/CB6a/CB8 full-size QN cases are bitwise-equal)
forensic.impact: 0 divergence on 12 well-posed cibersort cases incl. 50181x50; divergence only on this degenerate overlap (eset_tme_stad), magnitude <= 2.5e-04

forensic.root_cause: count2tpm_fast._filter_matrix_features: after excluding NA rows from the inf/variance checks it rebuilds the keep-mask as full_ok = np.ones(...) and writes only the NA-free rows' flags into it, so NA-containing rows are silently RE-ADDED by the final countMat.loc[ok]. The 3 injected all-NaN genes survive in the fast (original drops them via feature_manipulation).
forensic.damage: fast output has 3 extra bogus rows (symbols KMT2E, RP11-436A7.1, SEC22C - zero-valued after fillna) and a different row ORDER from tie-shuffling in remove_duplicate_genes; on the 48056 common symbols max abs diff is 1.46e-11 (last-bit), no cell > 1e-9
forensic.trigger: any count matrix containing NaN that goes through the all-numeric fast filter path (has_na=True); check_data-only (CT6, no NaN) and inf/zero-variance rows (CT8) are unaffected

ES5.variant: non-unique index input (merge-expansion path in both)
ES5.note: depends on ES1 inputs already built

forensic.root_cause: estimate_fast non-unique-index fallback: original computes set_indices = [gene_names.index(g) for g in overlap] (FIRST occurrence of each label); fast builds gene_pos = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(gene_names)} (LAST occurrence wins). With 300 duplicated index labels the merged frame has 61 duplicated gene labels; 1 StromalSignature gene (DDR2) and 4 ImmuneSignature genes (ADAM8, LPXN, NKG7, TYROBP) get a different member position -> different enrichment member mask -> different scores.
forensic.damage: max abs diff 46.69 on ESTIMATEScore (StromalSignature 11.99, ImmuneSignature 37.17, TumorPurity 0.0057); 40 differing cells of 40
forensic.trigger: only when input_df.index is non-unique (fast falls back to _filter_common_genes_ref); unique-index inputs (ES1-ES4, ES6 incl. NaN values) are bitwise-equal

CB11.variant: NaN rows incl one LM22-intersecting gene (expected: both error identically or documented divergence)

forensic.behavior: NaN rows reaching the solver: original raises ValueError('Input y contains NaN') from sklearn; fast raises Rust PanicException ('called Option::unwrap() on a None value'). Both fail, but with different exception types (no graceful ValueError, and a panic is an unsafe error contract).

CT10.variant: duplicated Ensembl IDs (50 rows duplicated, 5000-row subset seed 23)
orig_error: Length of values (4796) does not match length of index (4706)

forensic.behavior: duplicated Ensembl IDs: original CRASHES in tpm.insert (symbol_map.loc[tpm.index] expands on the duplicated index: 'Length of values (4796) does not match length of index (4706)'); the FAST SUCCEEDS (it inserts symbol_map.to_numpy() instead) and returns a 4706x10 result. Not a drop-in replacement for this input class: fast silently completes where the upstream raises.
